name: Social Withdrawal
summary: Pulling away from social interaction or group settings — which may reflect a genuine preference for solitude, or exhaustion and anxiety from social/sensory demands, and doesn't necessarily mean a lack of desire for connection.
triggers: Difficulty reading social cues (body language, tone, facial expression), making interaction exhausting
Sensory overload in group or noisy social settings
Past negative social experiences (bullying, rejection, misunderstanding)
Preference for predictable, low-demand activities over unstructured socializing
General anxiety or low energy for the effort socializing requires ('social masking' fatigue)

remedies.text: Structured, low-pressure social opportunities (one-on-one playdates, shared-interest clubs) rather than large unstructured groups
Social skills training or a program like Children's Friendship Training that explicitly teaches and practices specific social skills
Ask directly and gently whether the person wants more social contact — some withdrawal is a genuine, healthy preference, not a problem to fix
Connect with peer or online communities built around a shared interest, which can feel safer than open-ended socializing

sources.label: Kennedy Krieger Institute (IAN) - Social Skills Interventions: Getting to the Core of Autism
